content:
Implemented (this session). Added a side-workspace scraper plus a gated codegen test.

Files added:
  proto-blue/scripts/wildscrape/Cargo.toml             — separate workspace (like fuzz/), reqwest+regex+anyhow+clap
  proto-blue/scripts/wildscrape/src/main.rs            — scraper binary, ~280 LOC + 4 unit tests
  proto-blue/scripts/wildscrape/README.md              — usage + pipeline docs
  proto-blue/crates/proto-blue-codegen/src/main.rs     — added generate_types_from_wild_corpus test
  /.gitignore                                          — added /proto-blue/lexicons.wild/ + /proto-blue/scripts/wildscrape/target/

Pipeline (one-shot, idempotent, resumable):
  1. Fetch /browse HTML → enumerate top-level NSID prefixes (~85 TLDs at last count)
  2. Per TLD, paginate garden.lexicon.browse XRPC (limit=100, cursor) until exhausted
  3. Per NSID:
     a. /nsid/<nsid> → docs page → extract authority DID from canonical <link>
     b. /lexicon/<did>/<nsid> → schema page → extract <pre id=\"lexiconSchema\"> JSON
     c. HTML-decode and write lexicons.wild/<nsid>.json
     d. Validate JSON parses before writing (early extraction-bug detection)
  4. Skip already-present non-empty files for fast resume
  5. 50ms inter-fetch delay (configurable) for politeness

Flags:
  --output <DIR>                  default lexicons.wild
  --only <prefix1,prefix2,...>    skip discovery, scrape just these TLDs
  --delay-ms <MS>                 inter-fetch delay (default 50)
  --limit <N>                     stop after N new files (smoke-tests)

Codegen test (proto-blue-codegen tests::generate_types_from_wild_corpus):
  - If <workspace>/lexicons.wild/ is absent: skip with helpful message pointing at the scraper.
  - If present: load every JSON, run Generator, assert no panic + every leaf .rs file has the canonical //! Lexicon: header.
  - Does NOT compile the generated output — that's a heavier check for a follow-up nightly job.

Smoke-verified end-to-end: scraped 5 lexicons from the chat. prefix into /tmp/wildscrape-smoke, symlinked to lexicons.wild, ran the test, saw \"Wild corpus: loaded 5 lexicon document(s); generated 9 file(s) without panicking\". Cleaned up.

Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting):
  cargo build --workspace                                           PASS
  cargo test --workspace                                            PASS (67 suites, 0 failures)
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings             PASS
  cargo fmt --all --check                                           PASS
  scripts/wildscrape: cargo test --release                          PASS (4 unit tests for HTML/decode/regex extraction)
  scripts/wildscrape: cargo clippy --release --all-targets -- -D warnings   PASS
  scripts/wildscrape: cargo fmt --check                             PASS
  scripts/wildscrape: cargo run --release -- --only chat --limit 5  PASS (real network smoke; clean LexiconDoc JSON written)

Behavioural change: scraper is opt-in, never runs in CI without explicit invocation. Wild-corpus test is opt-in (skipped when corpus absent). No change to CI / per-PR builds.

Category: A (root-cause) — added the missing third-party-corpus validation pathway end-to-end (discovery, fetch, gated test, gitignore, docs).

Follow-ups (not in scope):
  - Nightly CI job that runs the scraper + the wild-corpus test (and ideally rustc-compiles the generated output to catch second-order errors). Worth a separate sub-issue under the audit epic if we want it.
  - The test currently asserts \"no panic + structural sanity\" only. A stronger version would invoke rustc against the synthetic crate; deferred per the README note.
